Thursday 24 · the regroup

Poker night

Good to regroup, and nice, for once, to get a poker session in on an away trip. Tricey continued his form with a dominating display. Ian had the hand of the evening, getting right inside Maff’s head with an outrageous – and entirely imaginary – ace-ten full house.

Friday 25 · Doña Julia · the CARTY

Jimmy holds firm

Jimmy took an early lead. Maff was up there with him for a spell – leading or sharing the lead after eight of the first eleven holes – but Jimmy was consistent throughout: never outside the top two, and clear on his own from the 12th.

Strong performances from Neil and Tricey, who shared the best back nine of the day with 20 points each. Tricey was last after the 1st and finished second.

Al had a day to forget. Nothing came quite right – 20 points, five pick-ups and the Lady to take home – and a few of the residents may come looking for reimbursement for some broken window panes.

A good day of CARTY, decided on the final hole. With one to play Jimmy led Tricey by a point, and Tricey had a hard birdie putt on the par-3 18th to force a putt-off. It stayed out, Jimmy’s position held firm, and he is a worthy winner, lifting the trophy for the second time – ten years after Edgbaston.

The head-to-heads · Reds 3½, Blues ½

A strong day for the Reds. Particularly impressive was Neil halving with the CARTY champion, especially as Jimmy has the better handicap these days: two down with three to play, Neil won the 16th and 17th to square it. Maff beat Al 5&4 – enough said. Ian beat Lee 3&2 and Tricey beat Zia 4&2.

above the line: the Red is up below: the Blue is upfaded: holes played after the match was decided

The boat race · Blues

A well-fought affair. Al wasn’t quite on his game this weekend and, unusually for him, spilled some of his Guinness down his top – but he still won his opening leg against Maff. The Reds fought back into a good position, with a great leg from Ian bringing them right back into it. But the Reds’ anchor, Tricey, for once had a disappointing anchor leg – although a stewards’ inquiry did look into how much was left in Zia’s pint at the end. Two points to the Blues, and Reds 3½, Blues 2½ overnight.

Then an outstanding pizza at Gold, and some good partying and karaoke.

Saturday 26 · Los Arqueros · the scramble

Lee’s day

Saturday brought the first ever CARTY team scramble, with 8 points on the table. One win from the two matches would do it for the Reds; the Blues needed a win and a half. As it happened, the Reds were dominated.

The newly crowned CARTY champion had left it all out on the field the day before, but the mercurial Zia found fairway after fairway with booming drives and outstanding irons to play well above his handicap – his drive was used on eight of the sixteen holes. Maff and Ian somehow stayed in it until the 16th, but it was a day to forget for these two, nowhere near their form of the day before. Jimmy and Zia won 3&2.

In the other match Al continued his run of bad form, not helped by a dose of Marbella belly. Dogged performances from the Reds pairing of Neil and Tricey kept it close – level after twelve – but Lee had a day to remember forever.

HoleParYdsSI 5315715 1

On the par-3 5th, having seen partner Al leave him needing a good one, Lee adjusted his club and took a six-iron draw at it. Tricey immediately suspected it might be in. Lee first went looking for his ball at the back of the green, and we all watched as they moved to the hole to find it in the middle of the cup. Ecstatic scenes for our keenest golfer – finally, his first ever ace.

That momentum carried the Blues through. They pulled away from the 13th to win 3&2 as well: 8 points to nil on the day, and the team cup, 10½–3½. And with that ended the points, and the golf, for CARTY ’26 Marbella.
